text:
BERT4Rec explicitly acknowledges the mismatch between reconstructing randomly masked history items and predicting a future item; inference appends a reserved mask and reads its final hidden state. Terminal-mask and reconstruction losses therefore share item/position embeddings, attention, feed-forward layers and the prediction head, but need not benefit next-item ranking equally. [BERT4Rec](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.06690). Relevant diagnostic foundations: [LESS, ICML 2024](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.04333) estimates influence using Adam-aware update directions; [Selective Task Group Updates, ICLR 2025](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.11986) measures proximal task affinity while accounting for shared and task-specific parameter learning. A [July 2026 research note](https://dhruvbpai.github.io/blog/optimizer-conditioned-attribution/) decomposes first-order behavioral change across parameter groups using optimizer-induced updates; useful methodology, not BERT4Rec validation evidence.

Suggested adaptation, rather than an established BERT4Rec result: keep the training mixture fixed and reserve user-disjoint training-prefix queries with hidden terminal targets. From identical model/optimizer states, compute virtual Adam updates for the full mixture and each branch-omission counterfactual, preserving moment state, clipping, learning rate and weight decay. Attribute their incremental effects by parameter group using ∇L_probe · (Δθ_full − Δθ_without_branch); negative values predict reduced probe loss. Group tied input/output embeddings together, then positions, attention, feed-forward layers, normalization and head parameters. Check selected estimates with actual probe-loss changes under temporary updates, restoring all state afterward. Use fixed negative candidates and report ranking changes alongside a differentiable ranking loss across several batches. Adam’s nonlinear update means branch contributions need not add up; simple preconditioned gradients remain approximations. These probes measure local transfer, not sustained generalization or improved macro validation HR@10.
